text: {"question":"When the SH0ES measurement of the Hubble constant is incorporated into the joint analysis of Planck, DESI BAO, supernovae, BBN, and ACT data, how does the posterior distribution of H0 shift for the standard ΛCDM model compared to the dark QCD model, and what does this imply about the relative preference for each model in light of the DESI BAO tension?","reference_answer":"Including SH0ES data moves the ΛCDM posterior for H0 upward, bringing it closer to the SH0ES value but still leaving a 2–3σ discrepancy with the DESI BAO measurements. In contrast, the dark QCD model’s posterior shifts less, remaining more consistent with the DESI BAO constraints and thus showing a relative preference over ΛCDM when the late‑time H0 measurement is added."}
